statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete. Search/product/deals route failures were executed and recorded as observed issues, not untested blockers.

page.framework: Amazon server-rendered MPA with legacy AUI/custom component bundles
page.notes: Representative public commerce templates. No credentials or purchases were used. Product/search routes intermittently returned WAF challenge pages; this is itself recorded as a core-flow/resilience issue. Authenticated account, post-payment and seller/admin surfaces were not covered because they require credentials or transactions and do not represent public templates.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Computed and screenshot comparison under dark emulation shows the same white cards/light content surfaces; html reports color-scheme normal.
Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the active hero image changed after seven seconds even though zero CSS animations were reported, so auto-advance continues.
Forced-colors screenshot keeps navigation, search, headings, links and product imagery visible with strong system contrast.
CSS inspection found zero view-transition rules; search/product navigation uses full document changes and exposed abrupt challenge-state swaps.
No parallax, scrollytelling, reveal animation, animation-timeline or scroll-timeline behavior was present on the exercised templates.
checkOutcomes.reason: No parallax, scrollytelling, reveal animation, animation-timeline or scroll-timeline behavior was present on the exercised templates.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The homepage uses script-driven carousels with no scroll-snap or overscroll rules found; movement is controlled by legacy carousel controls rather than platform gesture primitives.
Long storefront chrome remains static while scrolling; CSS inspection found no scroll-state query, timeline or progress affordance.
DOM inspection found 22 role=dialog overlays but no dialog/popover primitives and no effective anchor positioning or position-try rules.
Visible carousel arrows, section headings, skip links and a strong 3px keyboard outline cue movement and focus on the accessible routes.
Fresh-load homepage, cart and sign-in screenshots show core content immediately with no modal or consent interstitial covering it.
The homepage exposes 22 custom role=dialog elements but zero dialog, popover or details elements, indicating manual overlay semantics/dismissal.
The first viewport is dominated by two navigation bars, a large rotating ad and dense competing promotional cards rather than a clear content hierarchy.
At a 360px visual viewport the layout primitive reported no viewport meta, 1000px inner/scroll width and 640px horizontal overflow.
Live CSS contains multiple @container width rules that change reusable grid-card spans and ordering.
Focus is visible, but the first viewport probe found 4 of 61 controls below 24px in one dimension and the fixed 1000px mobile layout harms touch use.
Homepage search/navigation, deals headings, cart state and sign-in form each state their purpose and expose a clear next action.
Fresh-profile search and product-detail routes both stop at a “Continuar a Compras” anti-bot gate; the deals route also returned “Algo falló”, preventing a dependable browse-to-buy journey.
Empty cart, invalid sign-in and unknown-route states explain the state and provide sign-in, retry/home or corrective actions.
Lighthouse measured FCP 7.6s, LCP 20.5s and performance 0.56; a separate trace still measured LCP 2.74s, showing materially variable load performance.
Both desktop and mobile layout observers recorded CLS 0 with no shift entries; Lighthouse also reported CLS 0.
Trace recorded only 2 long tasks, longest 71.29ms, with 40.77ms total blocking time; Lighthouse TBT was 121ms.
HAR recorded 315 requests and 5.74MB transferred, including five parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets and 21 font requests.
Lighthouse estimated 465KiB unused JavaScript and 155KiB unused CSS, including 328KiB wasted in the WAF challenge script.
Lighthouse found invalid ARIA on the searchbox/carousel and a cart visible-label/accessibility-name mismatch; the image probe found 14 missing alt values.
Lighthouse color-contrast audit passed and forced-colors screenshot preserved text/control visibility.
Keyboard focus has a clear 3px outline, but the homepage has no H1 and Lighthouse found an accessibility tree/ARIA structure failure.
Desktop, forced-colors, cart and sign-in screenshots show readable body text, headings and controls without clipping on their intended layout.
Homepage and cart omit viewport meta; 360px capture renders a 1000px desktop layout and the probe found four sub-24px controls.
Lighthouse captured repeated console.error entries for late-loading modules and MIX rendering errors.
Doctype/UTF-8 are valid, but 87 of 100 images lack dimensions, 98 lack srcset and 99 use legacy formats.
Lighthouse reported deprecated Shared Storage usage and DevTools inspector issues.
Homepage and deals have descriptive titles and meta descriptions; title/description Lighthouse audits pass.
Lighthouse found javascript:void(0) anchors, and the homepage lacks viewport meta and overflows by 640px at a 360px visual viewport.
Homepage returns over HTTPS with a self-canonical; deals provides a canonical; robots permits ordinary crawling of these public routes.
No JSON-LD was present on the homepage or cart despite organization/store/entity content, reducing machine-readable rich-result context.
HTTPS is used, but CSP, HSTS and nosniff are absent; 6 of 7 cookies were flagged insecure and session-like cookies were not HttpOnly.
HAR attributed 307 requests and 5.53MB to non-main origins, while runtime evidence shows continuous detailed performance telemetry endpoints.
No permission prompt appeared on load; the real sign-in surface contains WebAuthn/passkey code and uses username autocomplete.
Headers primitive found no clickjacking defense, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy in addition to missing HSTS/CSP.
Browser screenshots with JavaScript disabled retain the homepage navigation, hero and promotional content, closely matching the rendered view.
Fresh browser sessions produce inconsistent route behavior: home/cart work, search/product show a challenge gate, and deals can render a generic server failure.
This commerce storefront is intrinsically online for live inventory, pricing and checkout; no installable/offline intent is declared and no manifest is linked.
checkOutcomes.reason: This commerce storefront is intrinsically online for live inventory, pricing and checkout; no installable/offline intent is declared and no manifest is linked.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The 404/server-failure surfaces clearly say what happened and offer retry, search or a homepage route rather than a blank shell.
html lang is es-mx, content is localized Spanish, controls use dir=auto where needed, and LTR reading order remains coherent.
Rendered prices use Mexican peso notation and Spanish offer/countdown labels appropriate to the es-MX storefront.
Representative public paths exposed countdown durations but no absolute user-entered or cross-time-zone event timestamps to validate.
checkOutcomes.reason: Representative public paths exposed countdown durations but no absolute user-entered or cross-time-zone event timestamps to validate.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Pricing/promotions are visibly labelled, sign-in states terms before continuation, and cart/account actions are explicitly named; no confirmshaming or forced continuity was observed.
Submitting the empty sign-in form shows a specific Spanish alert asking for mobile number or email without losing context.
The username field uses autocomplete=username, but the password input exists with an empty autocomplete attribute instead of current-password.
Cart and sign-in are clear, but the representative search/product routes are gated, so pricing-to-product-to-checkout continuity could not be completed reliably.
Of 100 images, 99 are legacy formats, 98 lack srcset, 87 lack dimensions and 86 below-fold images are not lazy-loaded.
The homepage makes 315 requests and emits detailed telemetry while idle; Lighthouse reports 465KiB unused JS and 155KiB unused CSS.
The 5.74MB load includes 5.53MB from non-main origins, 248 image requests and 21 font requests, disproportionate for the initial storefront viewport.
No WebMCP/agentic tool registration was found and robots.txt explicitly disallows major agent user-agents, despite the site being an agentic-commerce candidate.
No public summarisation or language-model task on the exercised storefront paths clearly requires on-device inference.
checkOutcomes.reason: No public summarisation or language-model task on the exercised storefront paths clearly requires on-device inference.

checkOutcomes.evidence: After ten carousel-next interactions, heap grew from 25.20MB/407,012 nodes to 27.42MB/413,845 nodes; the modest one-pass increase was concentrated in native/code rather than an obvious runaway constructor.
Runtime JS heap was 20.74MB with 2,595 DOM elements; snapshot self-size was 25-27MB, proportionate to a large commerce homepage.
Before/after heap summaries show no Detached* constructor among retained leaders and closure count changed only 20,546 to 20,587 after ten interactions.

paths.description: Storefront homepage, global navigation, discovery and promotional-content template.
Promotions/listing archetype; represents category and campaign listings.
Primary product-search journey using a representative query.
Representative product-detail route selected from a homepage offer.
Cart/checkout entry state, representing the pre-purchase transaction surface.
OAuth sign-in form reached from the homepage, including empty-submit validation.

findings.summary: Dark preference is ignored
findings.evidence: Computed and screenshot comparison under dark emulation shows the same white cards/light content surfaces; html reports color-scheme normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Add color-scheme: light dark and theme surfaces with prefers-color-scheme/light-dark().

findings.summary: Hero auto-advances despite reduced-motion
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the active hero image changed after seven seconds even though zero CSS animations were reported, so auto-advance continues.
findings.suggestedFix: Stop auto-advance and suppress non-essential motion inside prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

findings.summary: Route/state changes lack View Transitions
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found zero view-transition rules; search/product navigation uses full document changes and exposed abrupt challenge-state swaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt same/cross-document View Transitions with reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Legacy carousel interaction bypasses native gesture primitives
findings.evidence: The homepage uses script-driven carousels with no scroll-snap or overscroll rules found; movement is controlled by legacy carousel controls rather than platform gesture primitives.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-snap/overscroll and declarative transforms for carousel gestures.

findings.summary: Long-page chrome is not scroll-state aware
findings.evidence: Long storefront chrome remains static while scrolling; CSS inspection found no scroll-state query, timeline or progress affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state/container queries or a progress affordance to reduce persistent chrome.

findings.summary: Custom overlays lack robust anchored positioning
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found 22 role=dialog overlays but no dialog/popover primitives and no effective anchor positioning or position-try rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Use popover plus CSS anchor positioning and position-try fallbacks.

findings.summary: Overlays use custom role dialogs instead of native primitives
findings.evidence: The homepage exposes 22 custom role=dialog elements but zero dialog, popover or details elements, indicating manual overlay semantics/dismissal.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate transient UI to popover and modal workflows to dialog with declarative dismissal.

findings.summary: First viewport is crowded with competing chrome and promotions
findings.evidence: The first viewport is dominated by two navigation bars, a large rotating ad and dense competing promotional cards rather than a clear content hierarchy.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce persistent navigation/promotional density and establish one dominant task hierarchy.

findings.summary: Homepage does not reflow at 360px
findings.evidence: At a 360px visual viewport the layout primitive reported no viewport meta, 1000px inner/scroll width and 640px horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Add viewport meta and replace fixed 1000px sizing with intrinsic/fluid layouts.

findings.summary: Touch ergonomics are weakened by small targets and desktop scaling
findings.evidence: Focus is visible, but the first viewport probe found 4 of 61 controls below 24px in one dimension and the fixed 1000px mobile layout harms touch use.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise targets to at least 24px and test touch/keyboard layouts independently.

findings.summary: Anti-bot and server gates break product discovery
findings.evidence: Fresh-profile search and product-detail routes both stop at a “Continuar a Compras” anti-bot gate; the deals route also returned “Algo falló”, preventing a dependable browse-to-buy journey.
findings.suggestedFix: Make WAF challenges recover automatically or preserve the requested search/product route after one accessible verification.

findings.summary: LCP is slow and highly variable
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 7.6s, LCP 20.5s and performance 0.56; a separate trace still measured LCP 2.74s, showing materially variable load performance.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the hero/LCP resource, reduce challenge overhead and defer below-fold work.

findings.summary: Initial delivery is request-heavy and render-blocked
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 315 requests and 5.74MB transferred, including five parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets and 21 font requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate critical CSS/fonts, defer below-fold assets and shorten dependency chains.

findings.summary: Large unused JS and CSS payloads ship on first load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 465KiB unused JavaScript and 155KiB unused CSS, including 328KiB wasted in the WAF challenge script.
findings.suggestedFix: Split conditional features and remove unused/duplicate bundles.

findings.summary: ARIA/name and image-alt defects remain
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found invalid ARIA on the searchbox/carousel and a cart visible-label/accessibility-name mismatch; the image probe found 14 missing alt values.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct allowed ARIA, align visible/accessibility names and supply meaningful alt text.

findings.summary: Homepage lacks a coherent top-level heading/ARIA structure
findings.evidence: Keyboard focus has a clear 3px outline, but the homepage has no H1 and Lighthouse found an accessibility tree/ARIA structure failure.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one descriptive H1 and repair invalid carousel/search semantics while preserving visible focus.

findings.summary: Zoom/reflow support is broken by missing viewport metadata
findings.evidence: Homepage and cart omit viewport meta; 360px capture renders a 1000px desktop layout and the probe found four sub-24px controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a scalable viewport declaration and ensure 320-400px reflow without horizontal scrolling.

findings.summary: Production page logs rendering errors
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured repeated console.error entries for late-loading modules and MIX rendering errors.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix late module and MIX widget failures; keep expected diagnostics below console.error.

findings.summary: Image markup and delivery are structurally weak
findings.evidence: Doctype/UTF-8 are valid, but 87 of 100 images lack dimensions, 98 lack srcset and 99 use legacy formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve dimensions, add srcset/sizes and serve modern formats.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and inspector issues are present
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported deprecated Shared Storage usage and DevTools inspector issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated Shared Storage usage and resolve DevTools Issues-panel warnings.

findings.summary: Mobile and crawlability fundamentals fail
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found javascript:void(0) anchors, and the homepage lacks viewport meta and overflows by 640px at a 360px visual viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace javascript: anchors with real href/button semantics and add a responsive viewport/layout.

findings.summary: Store/entity metadata lacks JSON-LD
findings.evidence: No JSON-LD was present on the homepage or cart despite organization/store/entity content, reducing machine-readable rich-result context.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite and applicable offer/entity JSON-LD plus share metadata.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie flags are incomplete
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but CSP, HSTS and nosniff are absent; 6 of 7 cookies were flagged insecure and session-like cookies were not HttpOnly.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy CSP, HSTS and nosniff; set Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite cookies according to purpose.

findings.summary: Third-party-like delivery and telemetry footprint is excessive
findings.evidence: HAR attributed 307 requests and 5.53MB to non-main origins, while runtime evidence shows continuous detailed performance telemetry endpoints.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise/batch telemetry and reduce cross-origin asset/request volume.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent
findings.evidence: Headers primitive found no clickjacking defense, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy in addition to missing HSTS/CSP.
findings.suggestedFix: Add frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy and a restrictive Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Runtime behavior is inconsistent across core routes
findings.evidence: Fresh browser sessions produce inconsistent route behavior: home/cart work, search/product show a challenge gate, and deals can render a generic server failure.
findings.suggestedFix: Align WAF/error handling so search, deals and product templates recover without losing intent.

findings.summary: Password field omits autofill semantics
findings.evidence: The username field uses autocomplete=username, but the password input exists with an empty autocomplete attribute instead of current-password.
findings.suggestedFix: Set autocomplete=current-password while retaining passkey support.

findings.summary: Commercial flow cannot reliably reach product and checkout
findings.evidence: Cart and sign-in are clear, but the representative search/product routes are gated, so pricing-to-product-to-checkout continuity could not be completed reliably.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve search/product intent through verification and test the complete signed-out purchase path.

findings.summary: Homepage assets are not sustainably optimized
findings.evidence: Of 100 images, 99 are legacy formats, 98 lack srcset, 87 lack dimensions and 86 below-fold images are not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Use AVIF/WebP, responsive sources, dimensions and native lazy loading below fold.

findings.summary: Idle page performs wasteful delivery and telemetry work
findings.evidence: The homepage makes 315 requests and emits detailed telemetry while idle; Lighthouse reports 465KiB unused JS and 155KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer background fetches, batch analytics and conditionally load non-visible features.

findings.summary: Initial media and cross-origin budget is excessive
findings.evidence: The 5.74MB load includes 5.53MB from non-main origins, 248 image requests and 21 font requests, disproportionate for the initial storefront viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a purpose-based page-weight budget and defer most images/fonts until needed.

findings.summary: Agentic commerce capabilities are unavailable by policy and structure
findings.evidence: No WebMCP/agentic tool registration was found and robots.txt explicitly disallows major agent user-agents, despite the site being an agentic-commerce candidate.
findings.suggestedFix: Define safe WebMCP/agentic form tools and an explicit agent-access policy for product/search actions.
